name: Hana Petrov

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m from the Work Futures Panel, an independent group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. This is confidential. What is a usual workday like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and manage seven people who check travel expenses for a large company. I look at receipts, work out whether a claim meets the policy and call staff when a journey went wrong. I’ve led the team for eight years and know the ordinary cases as well as most managers. I like finding a missing receipt before payday; I dislike telling a worker that a genuine trip was denied because a form was filled in badly.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is home like, and how much room do you have if the pay changes?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My husband, Farid, runs a press at a local print works, and our children are eleven and fourteen. We have a mortgage and about five months of expenses saved; my pay is normal for this manager job and there are some similar offices nearby. I have a bachelor’s degree. I have never used an AI tool and prefer to see the receipt and policy line myself, even if it takes longer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team to keep a person looking at a disputed receipt. A little automatic sorting is fine, but a worker should not have to argue with a form for a train fare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My job should stay, and five months saved would carry us through an ordinary print-works slowdown. Farid has regular shifts, so I would rather keep doing this job carefully than chase a new system.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I’d keep the Tuesday claims review and ask the senior clerk to check rejected travel that lacks only one document. In the first year Farid and I would keep transferring 160 monthly into savings while both wages arrive as expected.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm. The mortgage is there, but our pay and reserve are steady in this picture.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say to a worker missing one receipt?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask whether the rail company can send a duplicate and hold the claim open for a week. A missing travel receipt is not the same as a false journey.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use the automatic sorter yourself?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not yet. I have never used AI, and I would first need to see how it treats old rejected claims.

say: A **person** should review disputed receipts before a form wrongly denies a real train fare.
I’d hold the **claim open** for a week while the worker requests a duplicate receipt.
think: My **claims job** remains in a plateau.
Five months saved and Farid’s shifts cover an **ordinary slowdown**.
I would rather do **careful work** than chase an unproven system.
do: Keep the **Tuesday claims review** and check simple missing-document rejections.
Save **160 monthly** while both wages arrive as expected.
feel: I feel **calm** about our work and reserve.
S0.quote: A missing travel receipt is not the same as a false journey.
fieldNote: She has **never used AI** and values the actual receipt.
Five months saved help with an **ordinary print slowdown**.
She leaves room for a **duplicate receipt** before rejecting a real trip.

steps.text: Keep Tuesday claims reviews and check rejected trips missing one document
Transfer 160 monthly to savings while both household wages arrive as expected

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say receipt checking and policy answers are exactly the work AI will take. Before changing our team, management should show mistakes from old claims and keep a person for disputed travel.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The easy claims could leave us with fewer staff, and one manager might cover several expense teams. I’m experienced, but my own post could go, and the nearby offices may be making the same calculation.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I’d ask our senior clerk to test forty old rejected claims with the software and list the genuine trips it would deny. In the first year I’d watch a paid demonstration and learn the review screen only if it correctly handles those forty; I’d ask HR for written staffing dates before accepting any transfer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious about my own pay and the people who bring us real travel problems. I can look at evidence, but I do not enjoy being pushed into a tool before it is ready.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you count as a bad result?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A genuine trip should not be denied because its receipt is in the wrong box. I would ask the clerk to keep the old decision beside the machine’s answer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If the tool passes, would you change your mind?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d learn the screen on paid time, slowly. I would still want a person named on every appeal.

say: I’d demand **old-claim errors** before staff changes.
Receipt checks and policy answers are the **first exposed tasks**.
think: A smaller team could make one manager cover several expense teams, removing **my post**.
Nearby offices may have **similar cuts** to their own expense teams.
do: Ask the clerk to test **forty rejected claims** and wait for those results before live use.
Learn the **review screen** on paid time only after a paid demonstration handles forty claims correctly.
feel: I feel **anxious** about my pay and staff.
S1.quote: A genuine trip should not be denied because its receipt is in the wrong box.
fieldNote: She delegates the first **software test** to a trusted clerk.
Her experience does not remove **manager-cut risk**.
She would learn only after **successful paid evidence**.

steps.text: Wait for the clerk’s forty-case results before using AI on expense claims
Learn review screen on paid time only after paid demonstration handles forty claims correctly

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask for closure dates, severance terms and a human address for disputed expenses. A worker who paid for a real trip should know who will answer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 could check receipts, read policy and answer staff better than I can, so I expect my post to end. Farid’s work at the press may last until hands-on robots arrive around 2031, but one wage will not cover our mortgage and the children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week Farid and I would freeze our planned kitchen purchase and keep the deposit in our account. Before 2028 I’d ask about posted mailroom jobs within the company and request written severance; in the first year after AGI arrives, I’d take a mailroom post only if its written wage covers my mortgage share and the shift ends before the children need collecting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m alarmed by the thought of losing my wage. Five months saved buys time to look, but I would lie awake over the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would a mailroom post be safe?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Moving parcels is hands-on until robots arrive around 2031 in this picture. Its sorting, route plans and messages face AGI in 2028, so I would not call it safe forever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if there is no posted mailroom vacancy?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would use the reserve for a measured search at nearby firms. I would not leave this payroll for a rumour from the corridor.

say: I’d demand **closure and severance dates** before the expense desk moves to software.
Staff need a **human expense contact** when a genuine trip is wrongly denied.
think: Farid’s press wage may last until **2031 robots**, but cannot cover us alone.
do: Freeze the **kitchen purchase** and keep its deposit.
Ask about **posted mailroom work** and move only with pay covering my mortgage share and school-compatible hours.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about losing my wage.
S2.quote: I would not leave this payroll for a rumour from the corridor.
fieldNote: She expects her **2028 desk job** to end.
Mailroom planning also faces **2028 AGI** before 2031 parcel robots.
The transfer needs **written pay** and pickup-compatible hours.

steps.text: Freeze the planned kitchen purchase and retain its deposit for mortgage bills
Ask about posted company mailroom vacancies before 2028
Take a mailroom post after 2028 only with mortgage-share pay and school-compatible shifts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say five years is enough for the company to show real internal openings and pay people while they learn a different job. A list of parcel-handling course names is not a paid mailroom offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could keep earning while our older child finishes school and search for a mailroom role before 2031. The route planning and paperwork in that role face AGI in 2031, while the parcel lifting faces robots around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In January 2027 I’d ask for the posted mailroom rota and a written wage, then meet Farid to compare them with our mortgage and school pickups. I’d take paid parcel-handling training only if the company offers an actual vacancy, and apply before 2031 only if the wage covers my mortgage share; after AGI arrives, I’d stay only while the firm pays people for hands-on parcel work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious, but five years lets me check the rota rather than make a rushed promise. I would not spend our reserve on a course with no job at the end.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make a rota workable?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Farid’s press shift starts early, so I need to be home when the younger child returns from school. A late mailroom shift would require a real childcare plan first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the posted wage is lower?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the expense job while it pays and look at other posted roles. I cannot trade a known paycheck for a badge that does not cover the mortgage.

say: I’d seek **real internal openings** before spending time on courses.
The company should **pay staff** while they learn a different job.
think: Physical parcel work faces **2034 robots** later.
I could keep **earning now** while our older child finishes school.
do: Check the **posted rota and wage** against mortgage and pickup.
Take **paid parcel training** only with a vacancy, then apply only with pay covering my mortgage share.
Stay in **mailroom work** after 2031 only while paid parcel handling remains.
feel: I feel **anxious** but can check the rota.
S3.quote: A list of parcel-handling course names is not a paid mailroom offer.
fieldNote: She ties any **training** to a real posted opening.
Mailroom paperwork is still **thinking work** at 2031 AGI.
Her shift needs a **childcare plan** and mortgage-covering wage.

steps.text: Compare posted mailroom rota and written wage with mortgage and school pickup
Complete paid parcel training only if the company offers an actual vacancy
Apply for posted mailroom work before 2031 only with mortgage-share pay and workable childcare

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say a decade lets the company tell people which expense jobs end and which paid openings actually exist. I would not accept a glossy promise instead of dates and wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 53 in 2036, with both children grown. We could reduce the mortgage while both incomes last, but my expense work and any mailroom paperwork still face 2036 AGI; hands-on parcels and Farid’s press face robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In January 2027 Farid and I would pay 200 extra monthly on the mortgage only while five months of savings stay untouched. I’d check the internal vacancy list every quarter and apply for a posted mailroom lead job before 2036 only if the written wage covers the mortgage and real parcel work is included; after AGI arrives, I’d stay only while the parcel work remains paid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy, with time to make the loan smaller. I do not want to learn a new title that still sits at the same exposed desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why keep five months untouched?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A broken press or a job gap could eat the reserve quickly. Paying more on the mortgage is useful only if we can still cover a surprise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move to another expense office?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if it paid us while we searched for a better route. The same receipt checks face 2036 AGI under a different company name.

say: I’d ask for **real paid openings** and dates before expense jobs end.
A glossy promise cannot replace **written wages** for a new role.
think: We could reduce the **mortgage** while both wages last.
Mailroom paperwork faces **2036 AI** before 2039 parcel robots.
do: Pay **200 extra monthly** only while five months saved remain untouched.
Check **vacancies quarterly** and apply only for mortgage-covering mailroom work with real parcels.
Keep the **mailroom role** after 2036 only while parcel work remains paid.
feel: I feel **uneasy** but can reduce debt.
S4.quote: The same receipt checks face 2036 AGI under a different company name.
fieldNote: She protects a **five-month reserve** before paying down debt.
She recognizes **mailroom paperwork** is not shelter from 2036 AGI.
The job needs **written pay** and physical parcel duties.

steps.text: Pay 200 extra monthly on mortgage only while five months of savings remain untouched
Check posted internal mailroom vacancies each quarter
Apply for mailroom lead before 2036 only with mortgage-covering wages and physical parcel duties

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because the expense desk could end before there is a real internal opening. Written severance, a posted wage and time to arrange school pickup would help. Five months saved gives us choices, not a second income.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask what happens to the worker who bought the train ticket before the claim system rejects it. A real journey does not disappear because a receipt sits in the wrong box.

headlineQuote: A real journey does not disappear because a receipt sits in the wrong box.
portrait: **Hana**, 43, is an experienced travel-expense manager with a bachelor’s degree.
Typical pay and **five months saved** support a mortgage and two school-age children.
She has **never used AI** and wants old claims checked before learning a new screen.
She considers **paid mailroom work** only with a real vacancy, adequate wage and workable pickup.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end her expense desk before an internal opening appears.
whatWouldHelp: **Written severance**, posted wages and school-pickup time would help her choose.
